Per workflow: table (one of the app's own tables; a framework table is refused, api({at:'schema'}) framework_tables), field, initial, states (optional list), transitions (from → to → { role?, when? }; role is one role or an any-of list), timeout (state → { after: 7d|24h|30m, to }), on_transition (entered state → hooks.yaml-style entries).

A transition's `when:` (and an on_transition entry's) is SQL over the row: `when: "tracking_number IS NOT NULL"`, `when: "amount <= 500 OR approver_id IS NOT NULL"`. Unmet or unevaluable → 422 `condition not met`. Semantics, NULLs and the columns available: api({at:'hooks'}) → when_conditions.

The state set is `states:` when declared (list terminal states there too), otherwise every state named in `transitions` (as a from or a to). With `states:`, the write gate and `benmore check` refuse an initial, transition, timeout or on_transition state that isn't listed; without it they refuse an initial, timeout or on_transition state no transition names (nothing could reach it). They also refuse keys the runtime ignores (a misspelled `timeouts:`, `roles:` on a transition - which would silently drop the role guard - or an unknown on_transition entry key), a timeout `after:` that isn't a duration, and a timeout on a table without an updated_at column (a timeout counts from updated_at). A file already deployed with such a problem still loads; the app logs a warning for each.

Timeouts are checked every minute. A timeout moves a row only if it is still in the timed-out state when the update runs, so a transition made in the meantime wins and the on_transition hooks fire once.

A new row starts in `initial`: every create path (POST, batch, NDJSON ingest, /api/_transaction) writes `initial` into the state column whatever the caller sent; on a single POST a different submitted value is listed in X-Stripped-Fields. With no `initial:` declared, a submitted value is dropped so the column default applies. Rows reach other states only through transitions. Give the column the same default in schema.prisma (`@default("pending")`): a row inserted by a flow, hook or SQL takes the column default, and the write gate refuses a default that differs from `initial:` (create_null_state).
`timeout` moves rows whose `updated_at` is older than `after` (checked every minute; the table needs an updated_at column) to `to` and fires that target state's on_transition hooks.
